title: A Resource-Constrained Evaluation of Fine-Tuned Deep Learning and Local Zero-Shot Vision-Language Models for Brain MRI Slice Classification
abstract: Abstract Fine-tuned deep learning (DL) classifiers report near-saturated performance on public brain MRI slice datasets, but dataset leakage, lack of patient-level metadata, and limited robustness evaluation restrict their interpretation. Concurrently, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) enable zero-shot image understanding, yet their unadapted zero-shot performance under local hardware constraints remains unverified. We conducted a paired evaluation comparing fine-tuned DL architectures (ResNet18, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, ViT-B/16) across three seeds against local zero-shot MLLMs (Qwen3-VL-2B/8B, MedGemma-4B) on a locked, leakage-screened 260-image four-class evaluation set using a single NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU (10 GB). We evaluated ImageNet pretraining on ResNet18, executed a 35,100-inference controlled corruption matrix across five synthetic transformations, and compiled a frozen 24-case Grad-CAM failure gallery. Fine-tuned ConvNeXt-Tiny achieved the highest mean Macro-F1 (0.9610 ± 0.0041), followed by EfficientNet-B0 (0.9531 ± 0.0069), pretrained ResNet18 (0.9476 ± 0.0024), and ViT-B/16 (0.9284 ± 0.0157). ImageNet pretraining exceeded scratch training by +0.0617 Macro-F1 (95% CI [0.0077, 0.1192]; scratch seed SD 0.0515), though scratch models exhibited marked seed-level initialization sensitivity. The strongest local zero-shot MLLM (Qwen3-VL-8B) reached Macro-F1 0.3991, yielding a large observed performance gap under the tested zero-shot, label-only setting (McNemar p < 0.001). Under corruptions, ConvNeXt-Tiny had the numerically lowest mean Macro-F1 drop (0.0253). Grad-CAM maps revealed spatial shifts during perturbation failures, though focal maps were also observed in misclassified cases. Under constrained local compute, which restricts deployable model parameter scale, the tested fine-tuned DL models substantially outperformed the unadapted zero-shot MLLMs evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning on this slice-level benchmark. High in-domain scores must be interpreted conservatively alongside dataset provenance, corruption sensitivity, and post-hoc explanation limits.

title: Clinical Efficacy of Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging and Proton Spectroscopy in the Evaluation of Complex Ring-Enhancing Intracranial Lesions: A Four-Case Series from Pacific International Hospital, Papua New Guinea
abstract: Abstract Background: Ring-enhancing lesions (RELs) remain a persistent diagnostic challenge in neuroradiology, as neoplastic, infectious, and granulomatous processes frequently overlap in their conventional MRI appearance. Accurate differentiation is critical for guiding management, particularly in resource-limited settings such as Papua New Guinea (PNG), where access to advanced neuroimaging is concentrated in a few centers and specialist manpower is limited. Study setting and design: This retrospective case series was conducted at Pacific International Hospital (PIH), Port Moresby, PNG, over four months (June–September 2026). Four brain MRI cases were included: three presenting as ring-enhancing masses, and one miscellaneous nerve sheath tumour at the craniocervical junction and C1–C2 level. Materials and methods: Of the four cases, two were referred from Port Moresby General Hospital and two were managed in-house at PIH. Conventional MRI sequences, supplemented by single-voxel MR spectroscopy (MRS) in selected cases, were used to evaluate metabolite profiles and to help differentiate primary brain tumour, metastatic disease, and infective processes such as tuberculoma. Results: One case, an 18-year-old male, demonstrated a cortical high-grade glioma with elevated choline-to-N-acetylaspartate (Cho/NAA >1.5) and choline-to-creatine (Cho/Cr >2) ratios, favouring a glial neoplasm despite an atypical age. A second case, a 29-year-old male with constitutional symptoms, showed multifocal ring-enhancing lesions with a preserved NAA peak and Cho/NAA <1, consistent with CNS tuberculoma and correlating with the clinical history. A third case demonstrated periventricular, splenial, and parieto-occipital rim-enhancing and serpentine lesions, radiologically indistinguishable between tuberculoma and neurosarcoidosis; tuberculoma was favoured on supporting clinical evidence. A fourth, miscellaneous case demonstrated a craniocervical/C1–C2 nerve sheath tumour with a characteristic dumbbell configuration on T2-FLAIR and post-contrast T1-weighted imaging. Conclusion: This first PNG-based series demonstrates the added diagnostic value of MRS in characterising ring-enhancing lesions and illustrates how strengthened referral pathways from provincial and district-level facilities to centres equipped with advanced imaging can accelerate diagnosis and improve management outcomes.

title: Probabilistic three-dimensional mineralogical characterisation of drill core using μXRF and XCT: application to the Nautanen North IOCG deposit
abstract: Abstract Accurate mineralogical characterisation of drill cores is important for quantifying variability and supporting geometallurgical interpretations. Conventional assays provide bulk elemental concentrations but do not preserve mineral distributions, whereas individual non-destructive methods provide only partial mineralogical information. In this study, a probabilistic integrated framework was developed for three-dimensional mineralogical mapping, using four drill-core samples from Nautanen North, northern Sweden, as a case study. Micro-X-ray fluorescence (µXRF) maps classified with the Advanced Mineral Identification and Characterization System (AMICS) were co-registered with corresponding X-ray computed tomography (XCT) surfaces to derive mineralogical labels, which were used as two-dimensional supervision for a deep learning segmentation model, with XCT responses as the input. Detailed mineralogy was consolidated into four XCT-supported classes: Matrix silicates, Quartz, Garnet and Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides. Generalisation was evaluated using nested leave-one-sample-out validation, and predicted class probabilities were calibrated to better reflect prediction reliability. The selected support-aware calibrated ensemble achieved a mean accuracy of 0.899 and a mean macro Dice coefficient of 0.583. Matrix silicates transferred most consistently, whereas the Fe-bearing sulphides and oxides class remained difficult to discriminate because of its heterogeneous and overlapping XCT responses. The calibrated ensemble was subsequently applied to predict the mineralogical classes within a half-core XCT volume. Predictions remained spatially coherent across the evaluated XCT volume, with high confidence, low normalised predictive entropy and high spatial agreement. The framework demonstrates the potential to extend targeted surface mineralogical observations into three-dimensional predictions of mineralogical classes, accompanied by class probabilities and uncertainty fields, that can support geometallurgical domain definition and the selection of suitable samples for additional mineralogical analysis or metallurgical testing.

title: Longitudinal Multi-Modality MRI–Ultrasound Cyst-Level Analysis of Polycystic Kidney Disease in a Feline Model: A Proof-of-Concept Study
abstract: Abstract Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) in Persian cats is commonly monitored using total kidney volume (TKV); however, this kidney-level metric does not capture heterogeneity in individual cyst dynamics. Here, a standardized longitudinal imaging framework integrating volumetric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with serial ultrasound (US) is presented, enabling cyst-level analysis in a feline PKD model followed over two years. MRI-based volumetry quantified individual cyst growth rates and identified structural coalescence events, defined as the persistent loss of visible boundaries between adjacent cysts without implying luminal communication. Serial US provided high-frequency temporal context and supported MRI-defined trends, rather than replacing MRI-based structural assessment. The analysis revealed marked asymmetric progression, with significant enlargement and coalescence of right-sided cysts, while left-sided cysts remained stable. This dual-modality approach demonstrates the feasibility of integrating volumetric MRI with serial ultrasound for longitudinal cyst-level analysis, enabling the identification of asymmetric progression and cyst-level structural remodeling that may be overlooked by kidney-level volumetrics alone. Although based on a single case, this study demonstrates the feasibility of a standardized MRI–ultrasound workflow and provides a methodological framework for future validation in larger cohorts.

title: Extension of the phenotypic spectrum of BMP1-related disorders through a novel homozygous variant identified in a foetus with intrauterine growth retardation
abstract: Abstract Background Osteogenesis imperfecta encompasses a heterogeneous group of heritable connective tissue disorders characterised by bone fragility and skeletal deformities. Autosomal recessive forms of OI may result from defects in the BMP1 gene, which encodes two main metalloproteinases, BMP1 and its longer isoform mTLD, both essential for type I procollagen processing. To date, BMP1 -related OI has only been reported postnatally. Results We report a complex homozygous BMP1 variant identified by prenatal whole-exome sequencing in a foetus presenting a polymalformative phenotype at gestational week 23 + 2.Ultrasound findings included severe intrauterine growth restriction, bilateral clubfeet, cranial bone anomalies, and signs of cerebral hypoplasia. At this developmental stage, histological examination did not show features of osteoporotic bone structure. A combination of molecular and biochemical strategies led us to characterise the variant and the consequences on BMP1 protein expression as its biological activity in the processing of several substrates. Functional in vitro assays demonstrated that the c.835A > G variant, located within the protease domain of BMP1, leads to (1) a deleterious missense substitution (p.Arg279Gly) affecting protease activity toward multiple BMP1 substrates, including procollagen I, thrombospondin-1, and chordin and (2) aberrant splicing, inducing exon 6 skipping, and a subsequent frameshift of the open reading frame. Conclusion This case broadens the phenotypic spectrum of BMP1 -related disorders and suggests a role for BMP1 in early human development beyond skeletal fragility. The findings support the inclusion of BMP1 in prenatal diagnosis gene panels for severe syndromic foetal presentations and underscore the importance of functional validation in variant interpretation.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Using Normal Lung Radiomics and Dosiomics to Predict Radiation Pneumonitis After Lung Cancer Radiotherapy
abstract: Abstract Objective This study aimed to develop and interpret machine learning models based on radiomics and dosiomics features extracted from normal lung tissue after excluding the planning target volume for predicting grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis within 6 months after radiotherapy. Methods A total of 232 patients with lung cancer who received radiotherapy between February 2023 and June 2025 were retrospectively enrolled and divided into a training set (n = 162) and a validation set (n = 70). The region of interest was defined as the whole lung excluding the planning target volume. Radiomics features were extracted from pretreatment contrast-enhanced simulation CT images, and dosiomics features were extracted from three-dimensional RT Dose files using the same normal lung region. After preprocessing, LASSO regression and random forest were used for feature selection, and their intersecting features were retained. Eleven machine learning models were trained using five-fold cross-validation and evaluated in the validation set. Model performance was assessed using AUC, classification metrics, confusion matrix, and decision curve analysis. Kernel SHAP was applied for global model interpretation. Results Among all patients, 97 developed grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis, with an overall incidence of 41.8%. From 214 extracted features, 18 radiomics and dosiomics features were selected for modeling. Validation-set AUCs ranged from 0.725 to 0.812. LASSO and linear discriminant analysis achieved the highest AUCs, both 0.812; the 95% CI for LASSO was 0.708–0.917. The final LASSO model showed an accuracy of 74.3%, sensitivity of 58.1%, and specificity of 87.2%. SHAP analysis indicated that first-order, shape, and texture features jointly contributed to model prediction. Conclusion Radiomics and dosiomics features from normal lung tissue may provide complementary information for predicting grade ≥ 2 radiation pneumonitis after lung cancer radiotherapy. The LASSO model showed favorable discrimination and interpretability in the validation set, but external validation is needed to further assess its stability and generalizability.

title: Fusing Radiomics and Ultrasonic Features: A Superior Nomogram for Diagnosing Cervical Tuberculous Lymphadenitis.
abstract: Objective This study aims to develop and validate a radiomics-based nomogram derived from ultrasound (US) images for differentiating cervical tuberculous lymphadenitis (CTL) from non-CTL in the pre-biopsy setting. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on 287 patients with biopsy-confirmed cervical lymphadenopathy (116 CTL and 171 non-CTL), all of whom underwent conventional US examinations. The US images were randomly split into training and validation cohorts at a 7:3 ratio. Radiomics features were extracted from manually delineated regions of interest (ROIs) using PyRadiomics. Features with intra- and inter-observer ICC > 0.75 were retained. Significant features were selected via t -test and LASSO regression. A radiomics score (radscore) was calculated, and a nomogram was constructed by integrating the radscore with US features (necrosis, heterogeneous, and posterior enhancement). Diagnostic performance was evaluated using ROC curves, calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the Hosmer-Lemeshow goodness-of-fit test. Results The nomogram demonstrated discriminative performance, with AUCs of 0.798 (95% CI: 0.738-0.858) in the training cohort and 0.756 (95% CI: 0.654-0.858) in the validation cohort. Its AUC was higher than that of the clinical US model (AUC: 0.764 (95% CI: 0.700-0.829) and 0.744 (95% CI: 0.640-0.847), respectively) and the radiomics-only model (AUC: 0.693 (95% CI: 0.621-0.765) and 0.611 (95% CI: 0.492-0.730), respectively). The AUC difference between the nomogram and the clinical US model was not statistically significant, but calibration and DCA confirmed its favorable clinical applicability and goodness of fit. Conclusion The US-based radiomics nomogram may help differentiate CTL from non-CTL and serve as an adjunct to pre-biopsy assessment. This approach shows promise for improving the pre-biopsy diagnostic workup of tuberculous lymphadenitis, although formal subgroup validation in pathologically early-stage cases is warranted in future studies. Unlike "black-box" machine learning models, this nomogram provides a clear display of each predictor's contribution, which makes the model easier to interpret.

title: Neonatal Gastric Perforation Temporally Associated with Nasogastric Tube Insertion: A Case Report.
abstract: Background Neonatal gastric perforation (NGP) is a rare but potentially life-threatening condition associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Approximately half of reported cases are idiopathic or spontaneous, while the remainder are attributed to identifiable causes, including congenital gastric wall defects, hypoxic-ischemic injury, and iatrogenic trauma related to nasogastric tube (NGT) insertion, particularly in premature and low-birth-weight infants. Early diagnosis and prompt surgical intervention are critical for improving outcomes. We report a case of gastric perforation temporally associated with nasogastric tube insertion in a preterm, small-for-gestational-age (SGA) neonate, highlighting the diagnostic challenge of distinguishing mechanical from ischemic etiologies, together with management and preventive considerations. Case presentation We describe a male preterm neonate, born at 34 weeks of gestation with a birth weight of 1.5 kg (small for gestational age), who developed acute abdominal distension and respiratory distress approximately 12 hours after nasogastric tube placement for enteral feeding. Abdominal radiography revealed significant pneumoperitoneum, indicating gastrointestinal perforation. Emergency exploratory laparotomy confirmed a 1-cm full-thickness gastric perforation along the greater curvature of the stomach. The perforation was repaired surgically, and the infant subsequently recovered with comprehensive postoperative intensive care management. Conclusion Clinicians should maintain a high index of suspicion for gastric perforation in neonates, particularly those born preterm or small for gestational age, who develop rapid abdominal distension, pneumoperitoneum, or signs of sepsis following nasogastric tube insertion. Because clinical and radiological findings alone often cannot reliably distinguish mechanical from ischemic causes, standardized insertion protocols, prompt radiological evaluation, and timely surgical intervention remain essential for improving survival and outcomes in this rare but serious condition.

title: Intracranial Mesenchymal Tumor with FET-CREB Gene Fusion: A Case Report of Late Recurrence.
abstract: Intracranial mesenchymal tumors with FET‑CREB fusion represent a rare tumor entity newly defined in the 5th edition of the WHO classification of central nervous system tumors. Due to overlapping morphological features, these neoplasms were previously diagnosed under different names, including intracranial angiomatoid fibrous histiocytoma and intracranial myxoid mesenchymal tumor. Clinically, they need to be differentiated from meningioma, high‑grade glioma, solitary fibrous tumor, and other intracranial neoplasms. Most supratentorial lesions achieve good outcomes after gross total resection, and tumor recurrence is considered uncommon. We present a 58‑year‑old female patient who experienced local tumor recurrence 27 months after complete resection of a primary supratentorial cystic mass located in the right temporoparieto‑occipital region. The primary lesion was predominantly cystic with minimal solid components. Microscopically, oval and spindle‑shaped tumor cells infiltrated the cystic wall without obvious brain parenchymal invasion, accompanied by linear hemosiderin deposition. Immunohistochemically, tumor cells were diffusely positive for vimentin, MUC4, CD99, synaptophysin, EMA, and ALK (D5F3). Focal positivity was observed for CD68 and broad‑spectrum cytokeratin. All other markers including SMA, MyoD1, HMB45, myogenin, TFE3, MelanA, SOX10, SSTR2, PR, GFAP, and Oligo2 were negative. INI1 expression was intact in all tumor nuclei. The Ki‑67 proliferation index increased from 5%-10% in the primary lesion to 10%-15% in the recurrent specimen. Both primary and recurrent tumors harbored identical EWSR1::ATF1 fusion confirmed by next‑generation sequencing and FISH analysis. The patient received no adjuvant therapy after the first operation, and delayed recurrence was detected during routine MRI follow‑up. A combination of radiological findings, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing is essential for accurate diagnosis of this rare tumor. This case describes late tumor recurrence in an adult patient with typical low‑risk features, including supratentorial location and complete surgical resection. Our findings expand the clinical and pathological spectrum of EWSR1::ATF1‑fused intracranial mesenchymal tumors. Long‑term imaging surveillance is necessary even for patients with favorable clinical factors. Standardized follow‑up protocols and optimal adjuvant treatment strategies remain undefined and require further validation in larger cohorts.

All other markers including SMA, MyoD1, HMB45, myogenin, TFE3, MelanA, SOX10, SSTR2, PR, GFAP, and Oligo2 were negative. INI1 expression was intact in all tumor nuclei. The Ki‑67 proliferation index increased from 5%-10% in the primary lesion to 10%-15% in the recurrent specimen. Both primary and recurrent tumors harbored identical EWSR1::ATF1 fusion confirmed by next‑generation sequencing and FISH analysis. The patient received no adjuvant therapy after the first operation, and delayed recurrence was detected during routine MRI follow‑up. A combination of radiological findings, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing is essential for accurate diagnosis of this rare tumor. This case describes late tumor recurrence in an adult patient with typical low‑risk features, including supratentorial location and complete surgical resection. Our findings expand the clinical and pathological spectrum of EWSR1::ATF1‑fused intracranial mesenchymal tumors. Long‑term imaging surveillance is necessary even for patients with favorable clinical factors. Standardized follow‑up protocols and optimal adjuvant treatment strategies remain undefined and require further validation in larger cohorts.

title: Miliary Brain Metastasis with Perivascular Enhancement in ALK-Positive Lung Cancer: A Rapid Recovery after Concurrent Lorlatinib and Whole-brain Radiotherapy.
abstract: Miliary brain enhancement presents a broad differential diagnosis, and its combination with perivascular enhancement (PVE) suggests inflammatory or infectious conditions. We herein report the case of a 30-year-old man with ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma who developed progressive nausea and impaired consciousness during corticosteroid therapy. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed miliary brain enhancement with PVE, initially suggesting infection; however, the cerebrospinal fluid and laboratory findings were negative. Brain metastases were suspected. Concurrent lorlatinib and whole-brain radiotherapy resulted in rapid clinical and radiological improvements. Metastatic disease should be considered in cases presenting with miliary brain enhancement and PVE, even when inflammatory or infectious conditions are suspected.

title: Comparison of Pointwise Encoding Time Reduction with Radial Acquisition (PETRA) MR-Angiography with conventional MR-Angiography-Sequences for Follow-Up of intracranial Aneurysms in a real-world cohort.
abstract: MRI follow-up of treated cerebral aneurysms is essential to detect remnants or reperfusion but contrast-enhanced MR-angiography (ceMRA) and TOF-MRA can be impaired by implant-related artifacts. Pointwise Encoding Time Reduction with Radial Acquisition MRA (PETRA) is a novel, non-contrast MRA technique with promising results for aneurysms treated with clipping or coiling. However, its performance in patients treated with other devices, including flow diverters and intrasaccular devices, remains unclear. This study aimed to compare PETRA with other MRA sequences with a particular focus on vessel visibility. Ninety-seven patients with 124 aneurysms treated with various endovascular devices or surgical clips were included. All patients underwent MRI including PETRA, TOF-MRA and ceMRA between September 2024 and February 2026. Three neuroradiologists independently rated aneurysm reperfusion, as well as image quality and the visibility of the parent artery and branching vessels, using 3-point scales. Artifact-related signal loss and signal reduction due to artifacts were measured in millimeters. Interrater reliability was determined using Fleiss Kappa. Vessel visibility was rated superior with PETRA compared to TOF-MRA, and comparable to ceMRA. Artifact-induced signal loss and impairment were highest with TOF-MRA, differing significantly from ceMRA and PETRA. Overall image quality was lowest with PETRA. Reperfusion detection did not differ among the MRA sequences. PETRA shows potential as a non-contrast MRA technique for follow-up of cerebral aneurysms, providing better vessel visibility than TOF and diagnostic performance comparable to ceMRA. However, its prolonged acquisition time and associated lower image quality currently limits clinical feasibility and real-world applicability. Further studies focusing on scan time reduction and cross-device performance are required.

title: Sex-Specific Regional Brain Morphometric Correlates of Neighborhood Socioeconomic Disadvantage in Clinical Neuroimaging.
abstract: Background and purpose Neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage is associated with adverse brain morphometry, yet whether these associations differ by biological sex remain opaque. Here, we investigated sex-specific associations between the area deprivation index and brain morphometry derived from routine clinical MRI in a real-world clinical population. Materials and methods Intracranial volume-normalized regional brain volumes were extracted from T1-weighted MRI examinations performed in 2,863 consecutive clinical patients (median age 54 years [IQR 38-68]; 61.2% female) at a single academic medical center and associated community partners using an automated atlas-based segmentation pipeline. Exploratory factor analysis was applied to 131 regional brain volumes to identify latent neuroanatomical morphometric networks. Sex-stratified and interaction linear regression models examined associations between area deprivation index national percentile rank and each factor score, adjusting for age, with correction for multiple comparisons. Results Factor analysis identified five neuroanatomical morphometric networks: cerebellar (ML1), frontal/executive (ML2), subcortical-ventricular (ML3), medial temporal/limbic (ML4), and posterior cortical/visual (ML5). In male patients ( n = 1,112), linear regressions revealed that greater neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage was significantly associated with lower factor scores on the cerebellar (β = -0.006, 95% CI [-0.009, -0.003], P < .001), medial temporal/limbic (β = -0.004, 95% CI [-0.007, -0.001], P = .01), and frontal/executive (β = -0.004, 95% CI [-0.007, -0.0004], P = .04) networks. No significant associations were observed in female patients (all P s ≥ .61). The interaction analysis was significant only for the cerebellar network (β = -0.005, 95% CI [-0.009, -0.001], P = .01; all other P s ≥ .07). Conclusions In a real-world clinical population, neighborhood-level socioeconomic disadvantage was associated with lower regional brain volumes across cerebellar, frontal/executive, and medial temporal/limbic neuroanatomical morphometric networks in male but not female patients; the cerebellar network was the only network to remain significant in interaction models. These findings suggest that the neuroanatomical correlates of neighborhood disadvantage may be sex-specific, and that sex-stratified analyses may be necessary to fully characterize the relationship between the social exposome and brain morphometry in clinical neuroimaging research.

title: Microstructural changes in deep gray nuclei following electroconvulsive therapy.
abstract: Background and purpose Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is efficacious for the treatment of major depressive disorder. However, its underlying mechanism of action remains debated and may involve neurogenesis, changes in axon/synaptic density or glial cells. Restriction spectrum imaging (RSI) is an MRI technique that can resolve subvoxel microstructure, separating intracellular water from extracellular water, which can be further partitioned into hindered and free water. This technique can be used to determine whether ECT affects cellular microstructure through changes in signal contributions. In the present study, we aim to determine how RSI metrics change following ECT and whether these metrics correlate with clinical improvement. Methods RSI analysis of the Perturbation of Depression Connectome (PDC 1.0) diffusion MRI data for healthy control and predominantly right unilateral ECT patients. MRI studies were undertaken at baseline, 1-week post-treatment and 3-months post ECT (follow-up). Results Following ECT, right-sided RSI metrics changed in cortical and subcortical brain regions including right amygdala and right hippocampus between baseline and post-treatment. The hindered water compartment increased, the free water compartment decreased, and the intracellular compartment was unchanged. Post-treatment, volume increased in the amygdala and hippocampus, which partially resolved at follow-up, while right amygdala extracellular indices persisted. Changes in clinical symptoms did not clearly relate to volumetric or diffusion changes. Conclusions RSI provides imaging biomarkers that suggest extracellular water shifts with corresponding volume changes to be the predominant effect of ECT. Transient and longer-term changes in glymphatic flow may be one of the contributing, underlying mechanisms of action for ECT.

title: Large Language Models in the Radiology Workflow: Current Applications, Challenges, and Future Perspectives.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have attracted increasing research interest in radiology owing to their capacity for natural language processing and, more recently, multimodal image-text reasoning. This review provides a clinically oriented overview of LLM applications across the radiology workflow, encompassing scan protocols, image interpretation, radiology reporting, and communication with patients and clinicians. Although the existing general-purpose multimodal LLMs show promise in diagnostic tasks, their image-interpretation performance is limited; they often prioritize textual context over visual information, and they are prone to hallucinations. In contrast, LLMs have demonstrated practical utility in radiology reporting, including structured radiology reporting, summarization, automated data extraction, and clinically meaningful report categorization. This review also discusses the reporting guidelines and performance evaluation methodologies specific to LLM research to promote more scientifically rigorous and reproducible studies in this rapidly evolving field. Finally, we outline the future directions for LLM research to support the responsible and effective integration of LLMs in radiology practice.

title: Generative AI in Radiotherapy Imaging: From Cross-Modality Synthesis to Foundation Model-Based Segmentation.
abstract: Imaging underpins nearly every stage of radiation therapy, yet the images obtained closest to treatment delivery are often the least reliable. Cone-beam CT is degraded by scatter artifacts and inaccurate Hounsfield unit values, whereas on-treatment MRI is limited by time constraints that preclude standard protocols. Generative artificial intelligence provides new solutions to these limitations. This review examines three areas of direct impact: cross-modality image synthesis, in which diffusion models generate CT-quality images foundation model-based segmentation and target delineation, where large-scale pretrained models generalize across modalities without task-specific retraining and multimodal architectures improve delineation by integrating imaging with clinical text; and generative approaches to post-treatment assessment. Persistent challenges, including image hallucinations, algorithmic biases, and data privacy, must be addressed before these tools can be deployed safely.

title: Continual Learning in Medical Image Analysis: Appropriate Use and Lifecycle Governance.
abstract: AI models for medical imaging are typically trained once and deployed unchanged; however, as scanners, protocols, and patient populations continue to evolve, model performance may degrade over time. Continual learning offers a way to incorporate newly acquired data while limiting the loss of previously learned diagnostic knowledge; therefore, it is particularly suited to clinical environments in which historical images cannot be freely retained or reused. This review outlines the continual learning scenarios and methodological families most relevant to radiology, examines when continual updating is preferable to periodic retraining or simple recalibration, and summarizes the applications in classification, segmentation, detection, and multi-joint radiographic grading. It then addresses the clinical constraints that determine feasibility: privacy and regulatory limits on data retention, delayed and noisy labels, class imbalance, and evaluation requirements beyond the average accuracy. Therefore, continual learning should be implemented as a governed, auditable maintenance process rather than as a single algorithmic choice.

title: Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model construction and quantitative analysis of retinal vein occlusion lesions using color fundus photographs.
abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is the second most common retinal vascular disease worldwide, affecting over 7 million people in China. Currently, the clinical diagnosis and severity assessment of RVO largely rely on the subjective judgment of physicians, leading to high rates of missed diagnosis at an early stage, insufficient quantitative assessment, and poor consistency during follow-up. Most existing RVO-related AI models only support classification diagnosis and lack multi-dimensional quantitative assessment capabilities. This study evaluated an existing AI system (EVisionAI) for automatic segmentation and quantitative analysis of RVO lesions based on color fundus photographs, using a dataset of 106 RVO eyes and 60 normal control eyes. The system can simultaneously extract three core indicators: lesion characteristics, vascular morphology, and fundus tessellation density. The results showed that the Dice coefficients of the AI for the segmentation of hemorrhage, hard exudate, and cotton-wool spots were all above 0.78. After adjusting for demographic factors and systemic vascular risk factors in a multivariable GEE model, there were significant associations between the total area of hemorrhage, vascular fractal dimension, and vascular density for RVO (all P < 0.05), suggesting these metrics as promising objective biomarkers for RVO evaluation. A diagnostic model based on these multidimensional indicators achieved a cross-validated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.951 (SD: 0.018) for distinguishing RVO eyes from healthy controls. In summary, the proposed AI system enables precise, standardized, and reproducible multi-parametric quantitative evaluation of RVO. However, given the single-center cross-sectional design and the absence of external validation and disease controls, these findings are preliminary. Prospective multi-center studies with external validation are required to confirm its clinical utility.

title: Incremental diagnostic value of coronary CT angiography-derived pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis.
abstract: Background Pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) radiomics may complement coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-based anatomical and physiological assessment. This study aimed to evaluate its incremental diagnostic value for identifying hemodynamically significant coronary stenosis. Methods This retrospective study screened 21,438 consecutive patients and included 81 patients with 107 target vessels who underwent CCTA, invasive coronary angiography, and invasive fractional flow reserve (FFR) measurement within 30 days. Patients were allocated at the patient level to training and validation cohorts in a 7:3 ratio. A radiomics score (Radscore) was developed from lesion-specific PCAT features using training-only preprocessing and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator logistic regression. Models incorporating diameter stenosis (DS), CCTA-derived FFR (CT-FFR), fat attenuation index (FAI), and Radscore were evaluated against invasive FFR ≤0.80 using patient-cluster bootstrap inference. Results The training and validation cohorts comprised 57 and 24 patients with 75 and 32 vessels, respectively, without patient overlap. In validation, Radscore alone had an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.684 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.451-0.873). CT-FFR+ Radscore showed higher discrimination than CT-FFR alone (AUC, 0.879 vs. 0.762; difference, 0.117; 95% CI, 0.005-0.229; P = 0.041), as did DS+ Radscore vs. DS alone (AUC, 0.812 vs. 0.619; difference, 0.193; 95% CI, 0.018-0.367; P = 0.030). The FAI comparison was not significant ( P = 0.238). At training-derived cutoffs, CT-FFR+ Radscore had lower sensitivity (50.0% vs. 78.6%) and negative predictive value (69.6% vs. 81.3%) but higher specificity (88.9% vs. 72.2%). Conclusions Adding Radscore was associated with higher discrimination for CT-FFR and DS in internal validation but did not uniformly improve threshold-dependent classification. Independent external validation is warranted.

title: Analysis of morphologic and morphometric features of the temporomandibular joint in patients with and without temporomandibular disorders.
abstract: Background Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are common craniofacial conditions characterized by pain and functional limitation. The study was conducted to investigate the association of morphology and morphometric features of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) with TMD using cone beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods This cross-sectional study evaluated 264 TMJs using CBCT of 132 patients within the age range of 18-60 years. The study comprised 66 patients with TMD in the study group and 66 patients without TMD in control group. Parameters analyzed included shape of condyle, glenoid fossa, bony changes, condylar height and width, joint space dimensions, roof of glenoid fossa(RGF) thickness, width and depth. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS version 26.0. Holm-Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Statistical significance was defined at an adjusted alpha level of <0.05. Effect sizes were calculated for all comparisons. Results Females predominated in both the study (66.7%) and control (69.7%) groups. Among TMD patients, 16.7% presented with muscle disorders, 42.4% with disc displacement, and 40.9% with joint disorders. Angle-shaped condyles were more frequent in TMD patients on the left side ( p = 0.037) and on the right side ( p = 0.12); however, after adjustment, p -values exceeded 0.05. Glenoid fossa morphology showed no significant bilateral differences. Degenerative changes were significantly associated with TMD ( p < 0.001). The RGF was significantly thinner in cases on the left ( p = 0.002) and right ( p = 0.007) sides. On comparison of the means of right and left morphometric parameters between cases and controls, reduced RGF in cases was statistically significant ( p = 0.008), and other parameters demonstrated no significant differences ( p > 0.05). Intra-examiner reliability was excellent (ICC > 0.94). Conclusion The present morphometric analysis revealed a significant association between reduced RGF thickness and TMDs, warranting further validation in longitudinal studies. Bilateral variations in TMJ morphology underscore the importance of assessing both sides independently, while degenerative changes detected in over one-third of patients highlight the value of CBCT in comprehensive evaluations. Importantly, the normative dataset generated here provides a regional anatomical reference for TMJ prosthesis design and supports CBCT-based evaluation in diagnosis, monitoring, and treatment planning.

title: Prediction of gross extrathyroidal extension in papillary thyroid carcinoma using a deep learning radiomics model based on post-processing techniques for multi-phase contrast-enhanced MRI images.
abstract: Background Gross extrathyroidal extension (ETE) affects surgical management and prognosis in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), yet noninvasive assessment is difficult. Methods In this retrospective exploratory feasibility study, 101 patients with pathologically confirmed PTC who underwent multi-phase contrast-enhanced MRI (MCE MRI) were analyzed. From the second and seventh contrast phases, four derived image types (ADD, ADD/SUB, Max, Min) were generated. Deep features from six image modalities were extracted using fine-tuned ResNet101, and radiomics classifiers were trained to predict gross ETE. Logistic regression identified independent clinical and MRI predictors, which, together with the deep learning radiomic signatures (DLR_signature) derived from the best-performing derived image type and algorithm, were integrated into a nomogram. Model performance was assessed by ROC, calibration, decision curve analysis, and ten-fold cross-validation. Results Gross ETE was present in 37/101 cases (36.6%). The Min-modality deep transfer learning model achieved AUCs of 0.852 (training) and 0.853 (validation); the corresponding radiomics classifier had AUCs of 0.870 and 0.805. Multivariate analysis identified mean apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC_mean) (P = 0.001) and protrusion_value (P < 0.001) as independent predictors. The integrated nomogram combining Min-modality DLR_signature, protrusion_value, and ADC_mean achieved AUCs of 0.956 (training) and 0.895 (validation), with average AUCs of 0.875 and 0.846 in cross-validation. Calibration and decision-curve analyses showed favorable performance in the current dataset. Conclusion The proposed nomogram integrating a Min-modality DLR_signature with quantitative MRI parameters showed promising potential for the noninvasive prediction of gross ETE in PTC. These findings support the feasibility of using MCE MRI post-processing for preoperative ETE prediction.

title: MambaGLA-NPC: a 3D framework integrating CNN and state space models for robust multi-center nasopharyngeal carcinoma segmentation.
abstract: Background and objective Accurate 3D segmentation of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) from MRI is critical for radiotherapy planning but remains challenging due to poor multi-center generalization, lack of spatial continuity, and high computational costs of global modeling. We aim to address these limitations by proposing a novel 3D framework. Methods We propose MambaGLA-NPC, a 3D deep learning framework integrating State Space Models (SSMs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) in a U-shaped encoder-decoder architecture. A Conv-GLSSM module jointly extracts static local features via convolutions and global context via SSMs with a 3D local scanning strategy. A gated channel-spatial attention (GCS Att) module suppresses irrelevant noise in skip connections, and an NPC-specific adapter enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning across multi-center datasets. Results On a multi-center dataset of 1,098 NPC patients from three hospitals, our model achieves state-of-the-art performance on the internal test set (Dice: 80.47%, IoU: 67.83%, HD95: 4.09 mm). Under cross-center evaluation, it significantly outperforms prior methods (e.g., Dice of 87.13% and 76.70% on two external centers). The NPC-Adapter boosts cross-center Dice by up to 8.84% compared to no adaptation. title: Absolute and lung volume-normalized deep learning-derived pulmonary vascular measures in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: distinct clinical associations and the role of lung volume in prognosis.
abstract: Introduction Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) has an unpredictable course and poor outcome, and lung function-based risk stratification remains incomplete. Whether absolute and lung volume-normalized deep learning-derived CT pulmonary vascular measurements show distinct associations with disease severity and mortality in patients with IPF remains unclear. Methods In this dual-center retrospective study, 118 adults with newly diagnosed IPF, including 57 from the Italian cohort and 61 from the French cohort, underwent baseline chest CT analyzed with a deep learning-based quantitative pipeline combining lung parenchyma (whole lung volume, WLV; fibrosis extent) and pulmonary vascular metrics (total blood volume, TBV; and derived BV 5 and BV >10 indices representing vessels with cross-sectional areas of <5 mm² and >10 mm²). Twenty subjects without lung disease served as a comparison group. Associations with fibrosis were assessed by Pearson correlation, mortality by multivariable Cox hazards models, and longitudinal lung function by linear mixed-effects models. Additional models examined the prognostic associations of vascular metrics after accounting for WLV. Results Compared with controls, IPF patients had lower WLV and higher absolute TBV. Relative TBV (normalized to WLV) correlated strongly with fibrosis, while absolute TBV showed weaker associations. Relative vascular metrics inversely related to baseline lung function, whereas absolute TBV showed no significant association. Baseline TBV, BV 5 , and BV >10 did not predict forced vital capacity (FVC) or diffusing capacity of the lung for CO trajectories, but higher WLV predicted better FVC over time. Over a median 7.8-year follow-up, 72 deaths occurred. In multivariable models, higher absolute TBV, lower-lobe BV, BV 5 , BV >10 , and WLV, but not normalized TBV, were associated with reduced mortality after adjustment for established clinical variables. These findings suggest that preservation of lung volume and pulmonary vascular volume may be associated with improved survival. However, the associations of absolute vascular metrics with mortality were substantially attenuated after additional adjustment for WLV. Conclusion Normalized and absolute pulmonary vascular metrics capture different aspects of IPF, with normalized measures associated with fibrosis burden and functional impairment, while absolute vascular volumes were associated with mortality, although this association was substantially attenuated after accounting for WLV. Absolute vascular volume may therefore partly reflect preserved lung volume rather than an independent prognostic effect. Prospective validation is warranted.

title: Predicting postpartum diastasis recti abdominis using early-pregnancy abdominal wall ultrasound radiomics.
abstract: Background Diastasis recti abdominis (DRA) affects abdominal wall stability and is associated with low back pain and pelvic floor dysfunction. Early identification of high-risk individuals is important for prevention and individualized management. Objective To develop and validate a clinical-radiomics model based on early-pregnancy two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound images for predicting DRA at 42 days postpartum and establishing a risk stratification system. Methods This prospective study included 428 pregnant women at 5-8 gestational weeks, randomly divided into training ( n = 300) and testing ( n = 128) cohorts. Radiomic features were extracted from ultrasound images of the rectus abdominis and linea alba to construct Radscore1 and Radscore2. These scores were integrated with early-pregnancy BMI and exercise habits to develop a combined model. Model performance was evaluated using AUC, 10-fold cross-validation, Hosmer-Lemeshow test, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. A risk scoring system was constructed from regression coefficients. Spearman correlation analysis assessed associations with postpartum inter-rectus distance (IRD). Results Radscore1, Radscore2, early-pregnancy BMI, and regular exercise were independently associated with DRA, with regular exercise showing a protective association. The combined model achieved AUCs of 0.892 and 0.859 in the training and testing cohorts, respectively. In the scoring system, BMI ≥24 kg/m², absence of exercise habits, Radscore1 ≥ 2.73, and Radscore2 ≥ 1.85 were assigned 1, 1, 3, and 1 points, respectively. DRA incidence increased significantly with risk level (trend test, P < 0.001). Radscore1, Radscore2, early-pregnancy BMI, and rectus abdominis thickness were positively correlated with postpartum IRD. Conclusion The clinical-radiomics model and risk scoring system accurately predicted DRA at 42 days postpartum and enabled early risk stratification, providing a quantitative basis for individualized intervention and follow-up. This is a single-center study; the findings require validation in independent multicenter cohorts before clinical implementation.

title: MedFuse: dual-stream fusion of convolutional and vision transformer-based features for enhanced medical image classification.
abstract: Introduction Medical image classification is fundamental to computer-aided diagnosis. Limited labeled samples, subtle inter-class differences, and heterogeneous lesion morphology make it difficult for a single representation to capture all relevant cues. This study investigates MedFuse, a simple dual-stream framework that combines convolutional neural network (CNN) features with representations from a pretrained vision foundation model (VFM). Methods The CNN branch is optimized on the target dataset to emphasize task-adaptive local texture and morphology, whereas the VFM branch is kept frozen to provide a stable global semantic representation. The two pooled feature vectors are concatenated and passed to a common classification head. Accordingly, MedFuse is positioned as a systematic and reproducible fusion baseline. The framework is evaluated across all 12 two-dimensional MedMNISTV2 subsets using multiple CNN-VFM backbone pairs and is compared with alternative weight- and attention-based fusion schemes. Results Simple late feature concatenation was competitive with, and often more stable than, more parameterized fusion modules across the evaluated settings. Moreover, increasing the size of the VFM backbone did not consistently improve classification performance. Discussion These findings demonstrate that frozen foundation-model representations can complement trainable convolutional features in small-scale medical image classification, while also showing that increased fusion complexity or larger VFM backbones does not necessarily translate into better performance. MedFuse therefore provides a simple and reproducible baseline for systematically studying CNN-VFM feature complementarity in medical image classification.

title: Case Report: Renal rupture and massive urine extravasation following flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: analysis of 4 cases and literature review.
abstract: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 4 patients who developed renal rupture and urinary extravasation after retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) in our hospital. Their clinical data, intraoperative findings, rescue procedures, and outcomes were reviewed, alongside a narrative literature review of relevant studies. For the literature review, we searched PubMed and CNKI databases using the terms "RIRS," "renal rupture," "urinary extravasation," "intrarenal pressure," and "ureteroscopic complications," without applying strict systematic selection criteria. Because these cases were collected over an extended period without a dedicated procedural registry, we did not attempt to calculate the overall incidence of this complication at our institution; rather, this series focuses on the clinical presentation, risk factors, and management strategies. We acknowledge that the small sample size, retrospective single-center design, and absence of a control group are inherent limitations of this case series. All 4 cases were successfully managed without mortality. The primary contributing factors included pre-existing moderate-to-severe hydronephrosis with thinning of the renal parenchyma ( n = 4), duplicated kidney ( n = 1), prior renal surgery ( n = 2), prolonged operative time (2.5 to 3.7 h), presumed elevated intrarenal pressure (inferred from poor outflow and prolonged operative time), and pre-existing urinary tract infection ( n = 1). Emergency interventions comprised broad-spectrum antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, percutaneous drainage of ascites (1,000-1,200 mL drained within 30 min in relevant cases), and selective renal artery embolization for active bleeding ( n = 1). All patients recovered and were discharged; follow-up imaging showed gradual resolution of perinephric hematoma and extravasation. Renal rupture with massive urinary extravasation is a rare but severe complication of RIRS. Key preventive measures, as suggested by the published literature, may include strict case selection, adequate preoperative infection control, preoperative ureteral stenting (generally for 7-14 days according to prior reports), efforts to keep intrarenal pressure below the commonly cited threshold of 30 mmHg, and limiting operative time to the generally recommended 60-90 min, alongside early intraoperative or postoperative detection via ultrasound or CT. This series underscores that early recognition, multidisciplinary collaboration, and timely intervention, including prompt drainage, intensive care support, and selective arterial embolization when indicated, are critical for successful management.

title: Automated radiomics pipeline integrating TotalSpineSeg for Pfirrmann grading of lumbar disc degeneration with SHAP-based interpretability.
abstract: Background Pfirrmann grading of lumbar disc degeneration (LDD) is constrained by inter-observer variability. Although radiomics enables objective quantification, the manual segmentation required by existing models is time-consuming and undermines feature reproducibility. TotalSpineSeg, an nnU-Net-based tool, allows fully automated segmentation, yet its integration with radiomics for Pfirrmann grading remains unexplored. This study aimed to develop an automated radiomics pipeline incorporating TotalSpineSeg for Pfirrmann grading of LDD, and to assess whether three-dimensional features contributed discriminative information beyond mid-sagittal two-dimensional radiomics, simple measurements, and frozen ResNet50 embeddings (ImageNet and RadImageNet). Interpretability analysis was applied to identify candidate imaging biomarkers. Methods Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data from 210 patients with LDD yielded 630 disc samples (L3-S1, Pfirrmann Grades I-V). Segmentation was performed automatically with TotalSpineSeg. Of 1,774 extracted radiomics features, 517 were retained through a multi-step selection process. Ten machine learning algorithms were evaluated using a patient-level 80:20 train-test split with 5-fold cross-validation, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was applied for feature interpretation. Results Automated segmentation averaged 6.9 s per case. The CatBoost model achieved a macro-averaged area under the curve (AUC) of 0.936 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.913-0.958) for three-dimensional radiomics, followed by mid-sagittal two-dimensional radiomics (0.916), frozen convolutional neural network (CNN) embeddings (RadImageNet, 0.874; ImageNet, 0.864), and the strongest simple measurement (0.760). For the three-dimensional model, sensitivity and specificity were 63.9% and 93.1%, grade-specific AUCs ranged from 0.876 to 0.978, and SHAP analysis identified the Laplacian of Gaussian first-order minimum, Flatness, and gray-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) Imc2 as candidate biomarkers. Conclusions Integrating TotalSpineSeg with radiomics offers an efficient and interpretable approach to Pfirrmann grading. Three-dimensional features contributed the greatest discriminative information, with a modest increment over two-dimensional radiomics and a significant advantage over simple measurements and frozen ResNet50 embeddings. The candidate biomarkers identified are pathophysiologically meaningful features for LDD assessment.

title: Artificial intelligence-based tongue image analysis for non-invasive screening of gastric cancer, precancerous lesions, and related gastrointestinal disorders: a systematic review.
abstract: Background Gastric cancer remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, largely because many cases are diagnosed at an advanced stage. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histopathological confirmation is the diagnostic gold standard, but its invasiveness, cost, and limited accessibility restrict population-level use. Artificial intelligence (AI)-based tongue-image analysis may provide an objective, low-cost, and non-invasive adjunct for pre-endoscopic risk stratification. Methods This systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA 2020 principles and was informed by diagnostic test accuracy and prediction-model reporting frameworks. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched from inception to 10 June 2026. Eligible studies were original investigations applying machine-learning or deep-learning methods to digital tongue images for gastric cancer, precancerous gastric lesions, or related gastrointestinal disorders and reporting at least one quantitative performance metric. Data were extracted on study design, sample size, target condition, reference standard, image-acquisition protocol, model architecture, validation strategy, diagnostic performance, calibration, interpretability, and risk of bias. A narrative synthesis was performed because of substantial heterogeneity. Results The search identified 139 records, of which 78 remained after duplicate removal. After title, abstract, and full-text screening, 9 studies published between 2018 and 2025 were included. The evidence covered gastric cancer, precancerous gastric lesions or high-risk gastric screening, and related gastrointestinal disorders. Models included logistic regression and XGBoost classifiers based on handcrafted features, convolutional neural networks, transformer-based architectures, segmentation-assisted pipelines, and multimodal models combining tongue images with clinical, questionnaire, biomarker, or microbiome data. Internally validated AUCs ranged from 0.61 to 0.99 across target conditions. External validation was reported in only three studies and generally showed performance degradation, particularly for precancerous gastric lesions. Calibration assessment was uncommon, and most studies did not report calibration curves, Brier scores, expected calibration error, or recalibration procedures. Conclusion AI-based tongue-image analysis is a promising but early-stage approach for non-invasive gastric disease screening. Current evidence supports its potential role as an adjunctive pre-endoscopic triage tool rather than a replacement for gastroscopy. Prospective external validation, standardized image acquisition, transparent model reporting, calibration assessment, and evaluation in diverse populations are required before clinical deployment. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261444857, PROSPERO CRD420261444857.

title: Multiparametric MRI-based radiomics for differentiating HER2-negative, HER2-low, and HER2-positive breast cancer.
abstract: Background Breast cancer stratification increasingly extends beyond conventional TNM staging and binary human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) classification. This shift is driven in part by the therapeutic relevance of HER2-low disease. We investigated whether multiparametric MRI-based radiomics could support pairwise discrimination among HER2-negative, HER2-low, and HER2-positive breast cancers. Methods This retrospective single-center study included 157 patients who underwent breast MRI on two 3.0-T scanners. Radiomic features were extracted from T2-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted, and subtraction T1-weighted images. Seven classifiers were compared after a stratified 8:2 training-test split. Model development, five-fold cross-validation, and model selection were confined to the training set, and the selected logistic regression model was evaluated on the untouched test set. Results Logistic regression had the highest mean training AUC across the three pairwise tasks (0.778) and was selected as the common final classifier. Test-set AUCs were 0.922 (95% CI, 0.750-1.000) for HER2-negative versus HER2-positive, 0.756 (95% CI, 0.529-0.938) for HER2-low versus HER2-positive, and 0.705 (95% CI, 0.493-0.893) for HER2-negative versus HER2-low classification. Conclusions Training-set model selection followed by independent test-set evaluation identified the strongest discrimination between HER2-negative and HER2-positive tumors. Performance was less reliable when HER2-low tumors were involved, particularly for HER2-negative versus HER2-low classification. These findings are exploratory and require independent multicenter validation.

title: Global research trends and hotspots in blood-based biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease: a bibliometric analysis.
abstract: Background Blood-based biomarkers (BBMs) are rapidly reshaping the diagnostic and translational landscape of Alzheimer's disease (AD), offering a scalable alternative to cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) assays and positron emission tomography (PET). This paper aims to conduct bibliometric analysis on the hotspots and trends in this field. Methods Publications addressing AD-related blood/plasma/serum biomarkers from 1 January 2011 to 29 November 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus. Only English-language articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the R package bibliometrix were used to evaluate publication trends, collaboration networks (countries, institutions, authors), co-cited journals and references, and keyword evolution. Results A total of 1,771 publications with 53,568 citations were included. Annual output rose steadily and accelerated after 2018, while 2025 records covered approximately the first 11 months of the year. The USA (795 publications) and China (478) were the most productive countries, whereas the UK and Sweden showed strong citation impact and collaboration intensity. The University of Gothenburg (263) and Sahlgrenska University Hospital (237) were the leading institutions. Henrik Zetterberg (218) and Kaj Blennow (185) were the most prolific authors. Co-citation analysis identified the NIA-AA biological research framework and validation studies of plasma amyloid-beta (Aβ) and plasma phosphorylated tau (p-tau) as the intellectual base. Keyword and burst analyses indicated a clear shift from early themes (e.g., proteomics and oxidative stress) toward clinically oriented topics, including plasma p-tau217/p-tau181, diagnostic performance, and implementation recommendations. Conclusion Research on AD BBMs has entered a phase of rapid growth and clinical translation. Plasma phosphorylated tau (especially p-tau217) is the leading biomarker for detecting AD-specific pathology. Plasma Aβ ratios play a supportive role in amyloid triage, while neurodegeneration (NfL) and astroglial (GFAP) markers provide complementary information for prognosis and monitoring. Future priorities include real-world implementation, assay standardization, and integration of multi-marker panels into biological diagnostic/staging frameworks.

title: Multimodal neuroimaging and electrophysiological signatures in amnestic mild cognitive impairment with different amyloid-β deposition status: correlations with cognitive function and diagnostic value.
abstract: Background Amnestic mild cognitive impairment (aMCI) is a heterogeneous transitional cognitive state between normal aging and dementia. Aβ positivity elevates dementia conversion risk but does not equate to prodromal Alzheimer's disease (AD), and not all Aβ-positive aMCI individuals progress to clinical AD dementia. Distinguishing Aβ-positive from Aβ-negative aMCI facilitates pathological subtyping rather than definitive early AD diagnosis. This cross-sectional study aimed to characterize scalp-level resting-state EEG and structural MRI signatures specific to Aβ-positive aMCI, explore their covariate-adjusted correlations with cognitive performance and regional Aβ burden, and develop an internally validated multimodal auxiliary classification model for Aβ stratification. Methods Fifty enrolled aMCI participants (30 Aβ-positive, 20 Aβ-negative) and 35 cognitively normal controls (NC) completed unified 20-min eyes-closed resting-state scalp EEG, 3.0 T structural MRI, 18 F-AV45 amyloid PET and 18 F-FDG cerebral metabolism PET examinations. Artifact-free scalp EEG spectral power and regional θ/α ratio were calculated via Welch spectral analysis; voxel-based morphometry (VBM) was adopted to quantify whole-brain gray matter volume. Covariate-controlled partial correlation corrected for multiple comparisons was applied to evaluate cross-modal associations among cortical Aβ SUVR load, cerebral glucose metabolism and domain-specific cognitive scores. A binary logistic regression classification model combining screened EEG and MRI markers was established, with DeLong test for ROC curve comparison and 1,000-bootstrap internal validation. Results (1) Relative to Aβ-negative aMCI and NC groups, the Aβ-positive subgroup presented significantly elevated whole-scalp θ relative power and scalp θ/α ratio, decreased scalp α and β relative power (all q < 0.05, FDR-corrected), with predominant scalp oscillatory alterations distributed over temporal, parietal and occipital scalp electrode clusters. The temporal scalp θ/α ratio yielded optimal classification performance for Aβ stratification (AUC = 0.875). (2) The Aβ-positive subgroup showed significant gray matter atrophy across 13 AD-vulnerable brain regions including bilateral fusiform gyrus, inferior parietal lobule, parahippocampal gyrus, precuneus and right entorhinal cortex (all q < 0.05), with the maximum effect size identified in the right precuneus (partial η 2 = 0.477, AUC = 0.778). (3) Within the Aβ-positive subgroup, the temporal scalp θ/α ratio was positively correlated with medial temporal Aβ SUVR ( r = 0.501, 95% CI [0.146, 0.732], q = 0.030); right precuneus gray matter volume was negatively correlated with multi-region cortical Aβ burden ( q < 0.05). Left parahippocampal gyrus volume was positively correlated with MoCA memory subscores ( r = 0.479, 95% CI [0.118, 0.709], q < 0.05). No significant associations between scalp EEG metrics and FDG glucose metabolism survived FDR correction. (4) The multimodal logistic regression model integrating temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume achieved favorable classification efficacy for Aβ-positive aMCI differentiation (AUC = 0.852, 95% CI [0.748, 0.955]), with good calibration and clinical net benefit based solely on internal bootstrap validation. Conclusion The temporal scalp θ/α ratio and right precuneus gray matter volume are promising candidate non-invasive auxiliary biomarkers for Aβ pathological stratification in aMCI, rather than validated clinical diagnostic biomarkers. The multimodal model provides supplementary subtyping value within this single-center cohort, while external multicenter validation is mandatory before clinical application. This cross-sectional dataset cannot support prediction of longitudinal progression to AD dementia.

title: Early hematoma expansion provides incremental prognostic information beyond admission characteristics for 6-month functional outcome after adult traumatic brain injury.
abstract: Background Early hematoma expansion (HE) reflects interval progression of traumatic intracranial hemorrhage, but its association with long-term outcome and its prognostic contribution beyond admission characteristics remain incompletely defined. We evaluated whether HE was independently associated with 6-month functional outcome and provided incremental prognostic information beyond admission characteristics. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 640 adults with traumatic brain injury, including 285 with HE. HE was determined from the first two in-hospital head computed tomography scans obtained within 48 h after injury and was defined as a new intracranial hemorrhagic lesion or an increase of >3 ml in total hemorrhage volume. Six-month outcome was assessed using the Glasgow Outcome Scale (1-3 unfavorable; 4-5 favorable). HE was added to a study-specific baseline model comprising age, admission Glasgow Coma Scale score, D-dimer, baseline hematoma volume, cerebral contusion, diffuse axonal injury, frontal lobe involvement, and long-bone fracture. Results At 6 months, 145 patients (22.7%) had an unfavorable outcome. HE was independently associated with a lower likelihood of favorable outcome (OR, 0.20; 95% CI, 0.10-0.42). Adding HE reduced the Akaike information criterion from 392.767 to 365.908 (likelihood-ratio P < 0.001) and increased the area under the curve from 0.920 to 0.929 (ΔAUC = 0.009; DeLong P = 0.0289). Prognostic heterogeneity remained among HE-positive patients. Conclusions Early HE is independently associated with 6-month functional outcome in adult patients with TBI. As a readily obtainable finding on routine serial CT, HE may help refine early prognostic assessment in patients with TBI.

title: AI-assisted 3D thoracic body composition analysis identifies candidate imaging markers associated with overall survival in older patients with lung cancer receiving radiotherapy.
abstract: Background Older patients with lung cancer receiving thoracic radiotherapy have heterogeneous outcomes that are not fully captured by conventional clinical descriptors. We evaluated whether artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted three-dimensional (3D) thoracic body-composition analysis of pretreatment radiotherapy simulation computed tomography (CT) could identify candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival. Methods This exploratory retrospective single-institution study included 88 patients aged 70 years or older who received thoracic radiotherapy for lung cancer between 2019 and 2021. Thoracic skeletal muscle and intermuscular fat were segmented using an AI-assisted workflow followed by expert review and Hounsfield unit-constrained refinement. Twelve knowledge-informed candidate groups were evaluated using conventional Cox regression. After marker selection, the selected marker pair was assessed in continuous form using bootstrap optimism correction, repeated five-fold cross-validation, and Uno's C-index. Penalized and alternative model-family analysis were performed as exploratory sensitivity analysis. Results During follow-up, 28 deaths occurred. In an 18-case internal technical validation subset, the raw AI contours achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.930 for thoracic skeletal muscle and 0.723 for intermuscular fat. For Group 12, intermuscular adiposity index (IAI) and attenuation-weighted thoracic muscle fraction (TMF) were the variables that met the univariable screening criterion; the resulting two-marker model met the discrimination threshold without problematic collinearity. When modeled together, IAI values above the cohort median (hazard ratio [HR], 2.78; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.25-6.18; P = 0.012) and TMF values above the cohort median (HR, 3.77; 95% CI, 1.52-9.32; P = 0.004) were associated with poorer overall survival. In continuous form, the selected marker pair had an optimism-corrected Harrell's C-index of 0.751 (95% CI, 0.661-0.849), a mean repeated cross-validation C-index of 0.753 ± 0.112, and Uno's C-index of 0.737. These performance estimates were conditional on prior marker selection. Conclusion AI-assisted analysis of routine radiotherapy simulation CT identified IAI and TMF as candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival in this clinically heterogeneous cohort. The findings are exploratory and require independent evaluation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts before clinical use.

In an 18-case internal technical validation subset, the raw AI contours achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.930 for thoracic skeletal muscle and 0.723 for intermuscular fat. For Group 12, intermuscular adiposity index (IAI) and attenuation-weighted thoracic muscle fraction (TMF) were the variables that met the univariable screening criterion; the resulting two-marker model met the discrimination threshold without problematic collinearity. When modeled together, IAI values above the cohort median (hazard ratio [HR], 2.78; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.25-6.18; P = 0.012) and TMF values above the cohort median (HR, 3.77; 95% CI, 1.52-9.32; P = 0.004) were associated with poorer overall survival. In continuous form, the selected marker pair had an optimism-corrected Harrell's C-index of 0.751 (95% CI, 0.661-0.849), a mean repeated cross-validation C-index of 0.753 ± 0.112, and Uno's C-index of 0.737. These performance estimates were conditional on prior marker selection.

Conclusion

AI-assisted analysis of routine radiotherapy simulation CT identified IAI and TMF as candidate body-composition imaging markers associated with overall survival in this clinically heterogeneous cohort. title: 5.0T multi-parametric diffusion MRI histogram analysis for prostate cancer pathology grading and adverse pathological factors.
abstract: Objective To evaluate 5.0-T ultra-high-field multi-parametric diffusion MRI (mp-dMRI) combined with histogram analysis for assessing the pathological grade, stage, and adverse pathological factors in prostate cancer (PCa). Methods This retrospective study included 138 patients with histopathologically confirmed PCa. All patients underwent preoperative 5.0-T MRI, including diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), and intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) sequences. Histogram parameters were extracted from parametric maps of the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), mean diffusivity (MD), mean kurtosis (MK), true diffusion coefficient (D), perfusion fraction (f), etc. using 3D Slicer software. Between-group comparisons were performed using the Mann-Whitney U test or the independent-samples t-test, as appropriate. Spearman's rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate the relationships between histogram parameters and both the ISUP grade group (ISUP GG) and pathological T stage (pT). Logistic regression was used for variable selection and model construction. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. Results Among the 138 patients, most histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between clinically significant PCa (csPCa) and clinically insignificant PCa (ciPCa). For distinguishing csPCa from ciPCa, D_90th percentile achieved the highest AUC among single parameters (0.756). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses identified ADC_mean, MD_Minimum, D_90th percentile, and f_Maximum as independent predictors across the DWI, DKI, and IVIM sequences. The combined model comprising these four parameters achieved an AUC of 0.809. After internal validation using bootstrap resampling (1,000 repetitions), the resulting AUC was 0.808, indicating good model robustness. Further correlation analysis showed that multiple histogram parameters of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f also demonstrated mild to moderate correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage. D_RMS and MD_skewness exhibited the strongest correlations with ISUP GG and pT stage, respectively ( r = -0.458 and r = 0.443, both P < 0.001). Finally, among the 60 surgical patients, multiple histogram features of ADC, MD, MK, D, and f differed significantly between patients with and without EPE, SVI, PSM, and PNI. Conclusion Quantitative histogram parameters derived from 5.0-T ultra-high-field mp-dMRI show promise for the non-invasive assessment of tumor aggressiveness and adverse prognostic factors in PCa.

title: Source-based morphometry analyses yield associations between large-scale structural brain networks and psychopathic traits in incarcerated adolescents.
abstract: Studies commonly report that youth with elevated psychopathic traits exhibit deficits within limbic and paralimbic regions, including reduced gray matter volume (GMV) in the amygdala, orbitofrontal cortex (OFC), and temporal pole. However, studies have also reported additional structural abnormalities in regions extending beyond limbic and paralimbic regions among youth with elevated psychopathic traits, including the middle frontal gyrus (MFG), inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), precuneus, inferior parietal lobule (IPL), and fusiform gyrus. This suggests youth with elevated psychopathic traits may be associated with deficits within large-scale structural networks. The current study investigated whether youth with elevated psychopathic traits were associated with such deficits through the use of source-based morphometry (SBM), a multivariate analysis of structural magnetic resonance imaging data. SBM uses Independent Component Analysis (ICA) to identify distinct sets of brain regions that form different large-scale structural networks. We investigated whether youth psychopathy scores, assessed via the Hare Psychopathy Checklist: Youth Version (PCL:YV), were associated with SBM loading coefficients among n = 413 incarcerated boys. Compared to participants scoring low on the PCL:YV, participants scoring high on the PCL:YV contributed less (i.e., exhibited reduced GMV) to large-scale structural networks containing limbic and paralimbic regions (e.g., the amygdala, insula, OFC, temporal pole, and posterior cingulate) and additional regions (e.g., the IFG, precuneus, IPL, and fusiform gyrus). Through the use of multivariate SBM analyses, the current study helps further improve our understanding of structural abnormalities among youth with elevated psychopathic traits.
